verdict.summary: Dropbox app creation is self-serve, but unrestricted production distribution requires a production-readiness review. Plan around reaching 50 linked users or assembling evidence for an early-review request before relying on public-scale OAuth onboarding.
verdict.activeEffort: Create the app, configure exact redirect URIs and least-privilege scopes, add branding and a privacy-policy URL, test the authorization flow, and submit detailed API-use information. For normal review, the app must first link 50 users; otherwise provide evidence and a detailed early-review explanation.
verdict.waitTime: Dropbox says it responds to nearly all production requests within a few business days; no guaranteed review SLA was found.
verdict.mainGate: Dropbox ordinarily will not review an app for production until it has linked at least 50 Dropbox users, unless Dropbox accepts an early-review request supported by evidence and a detailed explanation.

steps.title: Confirm authority and account eligibility

detail.text: If acting for an organization, you must be authorized to bind it to the Developer Terms, and you must not have had a Dropbox account previously terminated by Dropbox.

sources.quote: Developer must have authority to bind that organization to these Developer Terms, otherwise Developer must not use or access the DBX Platform.
Developer has not previously had a Dropbox account that Dropbox terminated

steps.title: Create the DBX Platform app

detail.text: Create and manage the app in the DBX Platform developer portal, selecting an API, the access type, and an app name.

sources.quote: The DBX Platform developer portal can be found at www.dropbox.com/developers . Here you can create and manage your DBX Platform apps
It walks you through three steps: choose an API, choose the type of access you need, and name your app.

steps.title: Prepare a privacy policy and initial scope rationale

detail.text: Draft a clear privacy policy covering collected data and its use or sharing, plus a least-privilege justification for every requested scope.

sources.quote: maintain this policy in compliance with all applicable privacy laws and regulations
use and disclose User Data only as authorized by the User and only as necessary for the functionality of the Developer App.
we strongly recommend deselecting the scopes your app doesn’t need, which results in better overall security and asking for less permissions from your users.

steps.title: Register exact OAuth redirect URIs

detail.text: Add every redirect URI before using it. Dropbox checks the authorization request's redirect_uri against registered values; the authorization reference requires an exact registered URI and HTTPS except for localhost.

sources.quote: You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application.
Dropbox checks that the specified redirect_uri parameter in your Authorization URL matches one of the registered values at authorization time.
This must be the exact URI registered under OAuth 2 on your app’s Settings tab in the Developer Console

steps.title: Configure only the scopes the app needs

detail.text: Console-selected scopes determine which API calls access tokens can execute. At authorization time, request a subset with the scope parameter when appropriate; omitting it requests all scopes selected in the Console.

sources.quote: The selected scopes are applied to your access token and determine which API calls your application is allowed to execute.
If this parameter is omitted, the authorization page will request all scopes selected on the Permissions tab.

steps.title: Choose OAuth token behavior and implement PKCE

detail.text: Implement authorization-code OAuth with PKCE using S256. Request token_access_type=offline only if the product needs refresh tokens for background or durable access; otherwise the default is online access.

sources.quote: Include a code_challenge_method and code_challenge in your authorization URL. The code challenge method may be S256 or plain . Using S256 is the recommended approach.
If omitted, this parameter defaults to online .

steps.title: Add branding and the privacy-policy URL

detail.text: Set the branding privacy-policy URL and add an app icon before applying for production.

sources.quote: The URL of your app’s privacy policy.
Before you apply, add an app icon on your app’s Branding tab.

steps.title: Use development status for initial integration testing

detail.text: New apps begin in development status, and initially only the app creator can authorize the app. Build and test the OAuth flow once credentials are available.

sources.quote: By default, all apps are created in the development state
Initially, your new app will only be authorized for you.

steps.title: Enable testers and collect valid links

detail.text: Enable additional users for testing or internal use. Development apps can link up to 500 total Dropbox users.

sources.quote: Clicking ‘Enable additional users’ will allow a limited number of additional users to link to you application for testing or internal use.
it can only be linked with up to 500 total Dropbox users

steps.title: Verify the OAuth endpoints used by the integration

detail.text: Use https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize as the authorization endpoint and https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token as the token endpoint.

sources.quote: https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize
https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token

steps.title: Prepare the production application narrative

detail.text: Draft detailed API-usage answers, scope justifications, and any early-review evidence. Dropbox says more information may speed approval and reviews whether requested permissions are unnecessarily broad for the app's functionality.

sources.quote: The more info you provide when applying, the faster we may be able to approve your app
we’ll review that your app doesn’t request an unnecessarily broad permission based on the functionality provided by the app.
please provide evidence and a detailed explanation under the Request early review field

steps.title: Request production status after 50 links or request early review

detail.text: Click Apply for production in the App configuration section of the app Settings tab. Dropbox normally does not review before 50 linked users; use the Request early review field with evidence and a detailed explanation if needed sooner.

sources.quote: click Apply for production in the App configuration section of your app’s Settings tab in the Developer Console
it will not be reviewed until your app has linked with at least 50 Dropbox users
please provide evidence and a detailed explanation under the Request early review field

steps.title: Wait for the production-readiness decision

detail.text: Dropbox performs a production-readiness review and can approve or deny the app. Dropbox says it responds to nearly all production requests within a few business days.

sources.quote: Your app will undergo a production readiness review by Dropbox and will either be approved or denied.
We respond to nearly all production requests within a few business days.

steps.effort: A few business days for nearly all requests

steps.title: Launch only after production approval

detail.text: A production-approved app can be linked by any number of Dropbox users. Its name can no longer be changed by the developer after production approval.

sources.quote: Once your app is approved for production status, any number of Dropbox users can link to your app.

gotchas.text: At 50 linked Dropbox users, the app has two weeks to apply for and receive production approval or Dropbox freezes further linking.

sources.quote: once your app links 50 Dropbox users, you will have two weeks to apply for and receive production status approval

gotchas.text: Removing linked users does not unfreeze a frozen app; production approval is the only stated way to unfreeze it.

sources.quote: the only way to unfreeze your app is to apply for and receive production status

gotchas.text: Dropbox can reject an app for failure to comply with its branding guidelines or Developer Terms.

sources.quote: It will be rejected if it doesn’t.

gotchas.text: The authorization endpoint probe returned: HTTP 302 -> /oauth2/authorize_error?client_id=probe-not-a-real-client&error_detail=Invalid+client_id%3A+%22probe-not-a-real-client%2 (mentions "client_id")
After production approval, developers cannot rename the app themselves.

sources.quote: If you have an app in production status that you need renamed, open an API support ticket and we can do it for you.

whenBlocked.text: If Dropbox denies production status, correct the feedback and resubmit for production review.

sources.quote: If your app is denied, feedback will be provided so that you can correct any issues and resubmit for production review.

whenBlocked.text: If the app is frozen after the 50-user trigger, obtain production approval; removing linked users will not unfreeze it.

sources.quote: the only way to unfreeze your app is to apply for and receive production status

whenBlocked.text: For a necessary rename of a production app, open an API support ticket.

sources.quote: If you have an app in production status that you need renamed, open an API support ticket and we can do it for you.

uncertain: Dropbox does not publish a guaranteed SLA for production-review decisions in the reviewed materials.
The reviewed materials do not state the decision criteria or expected timing for an early-review request.
The reviewed production-review documentation does not state whether production review has a fee.

verdict.summary: GitHub OAuth app registration is self-serve: create the app, configure exact callback URLs, and implement the authorization-code flow. Plan around organization-specific approval when users need organization resources; there is no documented GitHub-wide OAuth-app verification review.
verdict.activeEffort: Minutes to register, then normal OAuth implementation and testing effort.
verdict.waitTime: No provider-wide review timeline is documented; organization-owner approval timing depends on each organization.
verdict.mainGate: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions require an organization owner to approve the app before it can access that organization's protected resources.

steps.title: Choose the app owner

detail.text: Register the OAuth app under a personal account or an organization where you have administrative access. A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

sources.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.
A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app in GitHub settings

detail.text: In GitHub Settings, open Developer settings, select OAuth apps, and select New OAuth App.

sources.quote: In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps .
Click New OAuth App .

steps.title: Provide homepage and callback URLs

detail.text: Supply a full homepage URL and authorization callback URL. An OAuth app can have up to 10 callback URLs.

sources.quote: In "Homepage URL", type the full URL to your app's website.
In "Authorization callback URL", type the callback URL of your app.
You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

steps.title: Validate redirect-URI design

detail.text: Use an explicit registered redirect_uri and exact callback matching where possible. With wildcard matching disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match a configured callback URL; GitHub warns wildcard matching can expose the app to security risks.

sources.quote: redirect_uri string Strongly recommended The URL in your application where users will be sent after authorization.
When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
Enabling wildcard matching can expose your app to security risks, because it allows an attacker to send authorization codes to any subdomain or subdirectory of the callback URL.

steps.title: Select minimal scopes and token lifetime behavior

detail.text: Request only the scopes the app needs, as a space-delimited scope value. If the app needs renewable short-lived credentials, include offline_access; GitHub says this produces eight-hour access tokens and six-month refresh tokens.

sources.quote: scope string Context dependent A space-delimited list of scopes .
Include the offline_access scope in your authentication request, which triggers the short-lived token pattern.
they get an access token that lives for eight hours and a refresh token that's valid for six months.

steps.title: Implement authorization-code OAuth with state and PKCE

detail.text: Direct users to GitHub's authorization endpoint with the registered client_id, a random state value, requested scopes, and a registered redirect_uri. Abort the flow if returned state does not match. PKCE is supported and recommended; GitHub accepts only S256.

sources.quote: GET https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize
client_id string Required The client ID you received from GitHub when you registered .
state string Strongly recommended An unguessable random string. It is used to protect against cross-site request forgery attacks.
If the states don't match, then a third party created the request, and you should abort the process.
PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) is now supported and recommended for user authentication in OAuth and GitHub Apps.
Only the S256 code challenge method is accepted.

steps.title: Exchange the callback code promptly and test reauthorization behavior

detail.text: Exchange the authorization code at GitHub's token endpoint within 10 minutes. Test with a user who has not previously authorized the app because previously authorized users may not see the scope-consent screen.

sources.quote: The temporary code will expire after 10 minutes.
POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
For users who have authorized scopes for the application, the user won't be shown the OAuth authorization page with the list of scopes.

steps.title: Verify the authorization endpoint is reachable

detail.text: HTTP 302 -> https://github.com/login?client_id=probe-not-a-real-client&return_to=%2Flogin%2Foauth%2Fauthorize%3Fclient_id%3Dprobe-no (mentions "client_id")

steps.title: Request organization approval when organization resources are needed

detail.text: For organizations with OAuth app access restrictions enabled, users must request approval from an organization owner before authorizing the app. The owner reviews the application information and grants access in the organization's OAuth app policy settings.

sources.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators must request approval from an organization owner before they can authorize an OAuth app
After you review the information about the requested application, click Grant access.

steps.title: Do not wait for a GitHub-wide OAuth-app certification

detail.text: The reviewed documentation identifies organization-specific OAuth app approval, not a provider-wide OAuth-app verification or certification submission.

sources.quote: Organizations can choose which OAuth apps have access to their repositories and other resources by enabling OAuth app access restrictions.

steps.title: Use an externally accessible public app when serving external users

detail.text: If users outside the owning organization or enterprise need the app, make it public. An Enterprise Managed User-owned app that needs external users must be recreated outside the enterprise.

sources.quote: If your app is owned by an EMU account but needs to be accessed by users outside of your enterprise, you need to recreate the application outside of your enterprise.
If users outside of your organization and enterprise need to access the app, make it public.

steps.title: Operate within OAuth token and sign-in limits

detail.text: Handle token issuance capacity and reauthorization: OAuth apps are limited to 2,000 access-token requests per hour, and the next sign-in after ten sign-ins by one user in an hour requires reauthorization.

sources.quote: OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour .
If an app signs the user in ten times within one hour, the next sign in within the same hour will require re-authorization of the application.

gotchas.text: An unapproved OAuth app cannot access private organization resources or perform privileged create, update, or delete actions on public organization resources.

sources.quote: API access to private organization resources is not available for unapproved OAuth apps. In addition, there are no privileged create, update, or delete actions on public organization resources.

gotchas.text: New organizations have OAuth app access restrictions enabled by default.

sources.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default. Organization owners can disable OAuth app access restrictions at any time.

gotchas.text: PKCE is recommended but was not required by GitHub in its July 2025 announcement.

sources.quote: GitHub is not requiring PKCE for any authentication flow at this time

whenBlocked.text: If a user is blocked from authorizing access to organization resources, have them request organization-owner approval for the OAuth app.

sources.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators must request approval from an organization owner before they can authorize an OAuth app

whenBlocked.text: If an EMU-owned app must serve users outside its enterprise, recreate it outside the enterprise.

sources.quote: If your app is owned by an EMU account but needs to be accessed by users outside of your enterprise, you need to recreate the application outside of your enterprise.

whenBlocked.text: If token issuance is temporarily blocked, reduce or defer access-token requests because GitHub documents a 2,000-per-hour OAuth-app limit.

sources.quote: OAuth apps are subject to a rate limit of 2,000 access token requests per hour .

uncertain: No reviewed source states a provider-wide OAuth-app review timeline, because no provider-wide OAuth-app verification or certification process was identified.
No reviewed source states how a developer configures an OAuth app's public or private visibility in the GitHub console.
No reviewed source confirms whether the August 2026 offline_access token-refresh rollout applies to every existing OAuth app without additional console configuration.

verdict.summary: A send-only integration using gmail.send is materially easier than mailbox-reading Gmail access, but a public app still needs Google verification. Plan around a security assessment, its recurring cost, and a multi-week review if you request restricted Gmail scopes and store or transmit that data on your servers.
verdict.activeEffort: Set up the Google Cloud project and OAuth branding, verify a developer-owned domain, implement the OAuth flow, publish complete policy pages, and prepare scope justifications and a narrated end-to-end verification video.
verdict.waitTime: Google estimates 2–3 business days for brand verification, 10 business days for sensitive-scope verification, and six weeks for restricted-scope verification; the estimates are not guaranteed.
verdict.mainGate: Public applications requesting sensitive or restricted Gmail scopes must be verified; restricted-scope data stored or transmitted on developer servers additionally requires a security assessment.

steps.title: Create or select a Google Cloud project and open Google Auth Platform

detail.text: OAuth configuration pages are now under the dedicated Google Auth Platform navigation section rather than APIs & Services.

sources.quote: OAuth configuration pages previously lived in the APIs & Services section. Now, these pages have their own dedicated navigation section called Google Auth Platform

steps.title: Choose the audience

detail.text: Choose External for users with any Google Account; use Internal only when the project is associated with a Google Cloud Organization and access should be limited to its members.

sources.quote: Projects configured with a user type of External are available to any user with a Google Account.
Projects associated with a Google Cloud Organization can configure Internal users to limit authorization requests to members of the organization.

steps.title: Prepare homepage, privacy policy, and scope-use copy

detail.text: Draft a product homepage, privacy policy, user-data disclosure, and per-scope justification that explain only the user-facing Gmail features the app provides.

steps.title: Configure OAuth branding and authorized domains

detail.text: The homepage must be on a verified domain you own, describe the app rather than only provide login, and the privacy-policy URL on the homepage must match the consent-screen URL. Every authorized domain must be ownership-verified in Search Console by a project owner or editor.

sources.quote: The homepage must be hosted on a verified domain you own
The homepage must describe your app’s functionality to its users. Your homepage can not be only a login page
You must add the link of your privacy policy to your homepage and this link should match the link you added on your OAuth consent screen configuration
You must verify that you own all domains listed in your Authorized domains section of the OAuth consent screen editor.

steps.title: Select the narrowest Gmail scopes

detail.text: Use gmail.send for a send-only feature where possible. Avoid restricted gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata, and https://mail.google.com/ unless the feature actually requires their broader access; request mail.google.com only when immediate permanent deletion is needed.

sources.quote: Uygulamanızın ihtiyaç duyduğu minimum erişim düzeyini sağlayan kapsamları seçin.
以您的名义发送电子邮件。
仅当您的应用需要立即永久删除会话和消息（绕过“已删除邮件”文件夹）时，才请求此范围。

steps.title: Create a web OAuth client and record its secret

detail.text: Create application credentials after consent setup, configure an exact HTTPS redirect URI controlled by the app, and securely store the client secret when it is displayed because it is not shown again after the creation screen closes.

sources.quote: Sonraki adım Uygulamanız için erişim kimlik bilgileri oluşturun .
Once the creation screen is closed, the client secret will not be shown again.

steps.title: Add test users and test the complete authorization flow

detail.text: External projects in Testing require listed test users and are limited to 100 test users.

sources.quote: Kullanıcı türü için Harici 'yi seçtiyseniz test kullanıcıları ekleyin:
Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

steps.title: Build and exercise authorization, callback, token refresh, and Gmail API behavior

detail.text: The authorization endpoint responds with a missing-client_id error when called without required parameters.

sources.quote: HTTP 302 -> https://accounts.google.com/signin/oauth/error?authError=Cg9pbnZhbGlkX3JlcXVlc3QSIU1pc3NpbmcgcmVxdWlyZWQgcGFyYW1ldGVyOiB (mentions "client_id")

steps.title: Account for short-lived test authorization

detail.text: Test-user authorization and any offline refresh token expire seven days after consent when Gmail scopes are requested.

sources.quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent. If your OAuth client requests an offline access type and receives a refresh token, that token will also expire.
If your app requests any other OAuth scopes, then this exception does not apply.

steps.title: Prepare verification submission materials

detail.text: Prepare English scope justifications and a demo-video script showing the end-to-end app, OAuth grant, exact requested scopes, and the features that use each scope.

sources.quote: Must show the end-to-end flow of your app including the OAuth grant process
Must demonstrate the app functionalities that utilize the requested OAuth scopes
You must provide a detailed justification for your requested scope(s)

steps.title: Submit brand and scope verification

detail.text: Submit accurate identity, homepage, policy, video, and scope-use materials. Insufficient scope justification can result in rejection.

sources.quote: All apps that access Google APIs must verify that they accurately represent their identity and intent
If your justification is deemed insufficient, your app verification request may be rejected.

steps.title: Complete a security assessment if restricted data reaches your servers

detail.text: If the implementation stores or transmits restricted-scope Gmail data on developer servers, engage an independent assessor. Google charges no assessment fee, but the assessor's fee is agreed directly with the developer.

sources.quote: اگر داده‌های با گستره محدود را در سرورها ذخیره یا منتقل می‌کنید، باید ارزیابی امنیتی را تکمیل کنید.
Google does not charge the developer any fees for security assessment.
The cost for such a service is agreed on between the developer and the assessor without any involvement from Google.

steps.title: Await Google's verification decision

detail.text: Google reviews the verification submission; restricted-scope apps that require an assessment must be reassessed at least every 12 months after the assessor's Letter of Validation.

sources.quote: برنامه‌ها باید برای مطابقت مجدداً درستی‌سنجی شوند و حداقل هر ۱۲ ماه یک‌بار پس‌از تاریخ تأیید «نامه ارزیابی» (LOA) ارزیاب، ارزیابی امنیتی را تکمیل کنند.

steps.title: Publish the app after approval

detail.text: Select Publish app to place the project in production, and request only scopes approved for the app.

sources.quote: A project's publishing status is considered In production after selecting the Publish app button.
The scopes needs to be approved prior to making calls to them.

steps.title: Keep the OAuth client and approved scope set active

detail.text: Exercise the OAuth client at least every six months and obtain approval before adding sensitive or restricted scopes to production requests.

sources.quote: Starting in June, OAuth clients inactive for 6 months will be automatically deleted
This is caused by approved apps making requests to sensitive or restricted scopes that the app has not been approved for during the verification process.

gotchas.text: An unverified app requesting sensitive or restricted scopes displays an unverified-app warning and has a non-resettable lifetime cap of 100 new users; exhausting it can disable Google sign-in.

sources.quote: Google will display an Unverified apps warning message if your project's OAuth clients request authorization of scopes considered sensitive or restricted before your project has completed verification for those scopes.
the user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed.

Failure to get your app verified before making requests to sensitive or restricted scopes will result in your project's 100-new-user cap eventually getting exhausted and Google sign-in being disabled for your users.

gotchas.text: Gmail data must serve user-facing features and cannot be transferred or sold for advertising, market research, email-campaign tracking, or unrelated purposes.

sources.quote: 3rd-party apps accessing these APIs must use the data to provide user-facing features
may not transfer or sell the data for other purposes such as targeting ads, market research, email campaign tracking, and other unrelated purposes.

gotchas.text: If Google rejects requested sensitive or restricted scopes, OAuth access to those unapproved scopes stops working.

sources.quote: If the app has been rejected for sensitive or restricted scopes, users’ access to the unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes in the app via OAuth will no longer work.

whenBlocked.text: If scope verification is rejected, remove the unapproved scope or remediate the policy issue, then resubmit the required verification materials before requesting that scope again.

sources.quote: If the app has been rejected for sensitive or restricted scopes, users’ access to the unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes in the app via OAuth will no longer work.

whenBlocked.text: If a verified app is blocked for requesting a new sensitive or restricted scope, add the scope in Cloud Console and obtain approval before making calls that request it.

sources.quote: The scopes needs to be approved prior to making calls to them.

whenBlocked.text: If an inactive OAuth client is deleted, restore it within the stated 30-day restoration window.

sources.quote: Developers will be notified of deletion due to inactivity, and can restore clients up to 30 days after deletion.

uncertain: The reviewed sources provide non-guaranteed stage estimates but do not state a fixed end-to-end verification timeline.
The reviewed sources do not specify independent-assessor pricing or how long a security assessment takes.
The reviewed material does not establish detailed architectural boundaries for when a restricted-scope implementation is considered to store or transmit data on developer servers.

verdict.summary: Customer ad-account access requires a verified business plus App Review approval for Full access to ads_read and/or ads_management. Plan around a development-only launch first: Full Marketing API access also requires 500+ API calls in 15 days with an error rate below 15%, and Meta publishes no review timeline.
verdict.activeEffort: Create and configure the app, complete Business Verification, build a reviewer-accessible OAuth flow, request per-permission advanced access, and generate reliable development-tier Marketing API usage.
verdict.waitTime: Unstated; Meta's reviewed documentation gives no Business Verification or App Review processing-time SLA.
verdict.mainGate: Business Verification and App Review for Full access to customer ad accounts, followed by Marketing API tier qualification.

steps.title: Register as a Meta developer and create the app

detail.text: You must be registered and logged in as a Meta developer, then create the app from the app-creation flow with an app name and contact email.

sources.quote: To create an app with Meta, you must first register as a developer and be logged into your developer account.
Navigate to **[https://developers.facebook.com/apps/creation/](https://developers.facebook.com/apps/creation/)** to begin the app creation process.
Enter your **app's name** and a **contact email address**.

steps.title: Choose use cases conservatively

detail.text: Select only compatible use cases you intend to support, because use cases cannot be removed after app creation.

sources.quote: **Use cases cannot be removed** after you create your app.

steps.title: Connect a business portfolio

detail.text: Connect the app to a business portfolio because an app connecting customers' ad accounts accesses data the app owner does not own or manage.

sources.quote: If your app will access data that you don't own or manage, you must connect your app to a business portfolio.

steps.title: Add Facebook Login and Marketing API

detail.text: Adding the Marketing API product gives the app Limited tier access by default.

sources.quote: When you add the Marketing API product in your [App Dashboard](https://developers.facebook.com/apps), you will get the **Limited tier** of Marketing API Access Tier by default.

steps.title: Register fixed OAuth redirect URIs

detail.text: Enter every callback under Facebook Login Client OAuth Settings. Each redirect URI must exactly match the registered URI, including query parameters except state; use state for dynamic post-login destinations.

sources.quote: Verify the **Valid OAuth redirect URIs** in the **Client OAuth Settings** section.
The full URI must be an exact match, including all parameters, with the exception of the optional state parameter, the value of which is ignored.
For apps with **dynamic redirect URIs**, use the [state parameter](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/facebook-login/guides/advanced/manual-flow#logindialog)

steps.title: Validate redirect-URI design and OAuth scope rationale

detail.text: Prepare a fixed redirect-URI allowlist, state-handling design, and least-privilege justification for public_profile plus ads_read and/or ads_management.

sources.quote: `scope`. A comma or space separated list of [Permissions](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/permissions) to request from the person using your app.
If you're managing someone's ads, use the `scope` parameter to prompt them for the `ads_management` or `ads_read` permissions.

steps.title: Request only required permissions

detail.text: Use ads_read for read-only customer-ad-account workflows and ads_management only where the product manages ads; public_profile is always required.

sources.quote: If you're managing someone's ads, use the `scope` parameter to prompt them for the `ads_management` or `ads_read` permissions.
The `public_profile` permission is always required and greyed out because it can't be disabled.

steps.title: Build and test the OAuth flow with app-role access

detail.text: Build and test the OAuth authorization-code flow after credentials exist, using app-role users because App Review is required before people without an app or connected-business role can use the app.

sources.quote: It is required if your app will be used by people without a role on your app or a role on the business that is connected to your app.

steps.title: Do not rely on newly created test users

detail.text: Plan testing around existing app-role users: apps are limited to 10 test users and Meta says new test-user creation is temporarily unavailable.

sources.quote: Apps are limited to 10 test users.
We are temporarily removing the ability for apps to create new test users.

steps.title: Operate within development-tier limits

detail.text: Treat Limited access as development-only. Under ads_management, development tier starts at 300 requests per hour per ad account plus active-ad scaling; its API-level maximum score is 60 and reaching it causes a 300-second block.

sources.quote: Heavily rate-limited per ad account. For development only. Not for production apps running for live advertisers.
`ads_management` - For each ad account in a one-hour time period: (100000 if your app is in the Marketing API Full access or 300 if your app is in the Dev tier) + 40 * Num of Active ads.
Your maximum score is 60.
You will be blocked for 300 seconds if you reach the maximum score.

steps.title: Complete Business Verification

detail.text: Complete Business Verification for advanced permission access and for an app that lets other businesses access their own data. Start from App Dashboard Settings > Basic > Verification, then finish the process in Facebook Business Manager.

sources.quote: Apps that request advanced access for permissions and apps that allow other Businesses to access their own data must be connected to a Business that has completed Business Verification.
Load your app in the App Dashboard and go to **Settings** > **Basic** > **Verification** and click the Start Verification button
the verification process itself must be completed in the Facebook Business Manager.

verdict.summary: A custom app for your own organization’s stores is comparatively self-serve, while a public App Store app needs Shopify approval and a one-time App Store registration fee. Plan around an unspecified review wait, and treat protected customer data—especially direct identifiers—as an additional approval gate.
verdict.activeEffort: Create and configure the app, implement OAuth, select only necessary scopes, test on a development store, and prepare a production-ready App Store submission if distributing publicly.
verdict.waitTime: No approval SLA is stated in the cited review documentation.
verdict.mainGate: Public distribution requires Shopify approval; protected customer data or other sensitive information also requires approval.

steps.title: Confirm the intended distribution model before creating the app

detail.text: Choose the distribution method carefully because Shopify does not allow it to be changed after selection. Public apps can install on multiple Shopify stores and require Shopify approval; custom apps are for one store, stores in the same Plus organization, or development stores and do not require approval.

sources.quote: Public distribution Can be installed on multiple Shopify stores
Public distribution requires Shopify approval.
You can't change the distribution method after you select it.

steps.title: Create the app in Dev Dashboard

detail.text: Create the Shopify app in Dev Dashboard. You need app-development permission; a Partner organization is not required to use Dev Dashboard.

sources.quote: You can create a new Shopify app right from your Dev Dashboard.
You're a user with app development permissions.
You don't need a Partner organization to use the Dev Dashboard.

steps.title: Set the app URL and choose least-privilege scopes

detail.text: For a standalone or API-only app, redirect the merchant to Shopify for approval, then exchange the returned code for an access token. The authorization request includes client_id, scope, redirect_uri, and state.

sources.quote: Because they can't use ID tokens , they authenticate using the OAuth authorization code grant flow: redirect the merchant to Shopify, get their approval, and exchange a code for an access token.

client_id : CLIENT_ID ,

verdict.summary: Spotify OAuth is easy to prototype for up to five allowlisted users, but public production access is partner-gated. Plan around remaining in Development Mode unless you are an established organization with a launched, commercially viable service and at least 250,000 MAUs.
verdict.activeEffort: Prepare a launched service, compliant product materials, efficient API usage, and a partner application; Spotify reviews app information, images, APIs/SDKs, Terms compliance, and the working app.
verdict.waitTime: Spotify says extended-quota review can take up to six weeks, with possible back-and-forth during review.
verdict.mainGate: Extended Quota Mode applications are accepted only from organizations and require a legally registered entity, an active launched service, and at least 250,000 MAUs.

Being available in key Spotify markets
